Opportunity cost is what you give up to produce something. So, in this case, for each barrel of wine, each country gives up some amount of cloth. The country that gives up less cloth per barrel has the comparative advantage in wine.

- So, if they want to make one barrel of wine, how much cloth are they giving up?
- To find that, I can calculate the opportunity cost. If they choose wine over cloth, they lose the ability to produce 20 bolts of cloth over 10 barrels of wine.
